title: Disable automatic updates for portable builds
description:
This change updates the software update behavior for portable builds of Wireshark on Windows and macOS. Portable builds will no longer attempt to use the standard update mechanisms (WinSparkle or Sparkle), which are intended for full installer versions.
What this MR does:
- Adds checks in software_update.c to disable automatic updates for portable builds.
- Preserves standard update behavior for non-portable builds.
Motivation / Issue
Addresses the behavior described in #20867 where portable versions attempt to download the full installer.

Notes
- No other changes to the software update logic are made.
- Fully compatible with existing prefs and localization code.

mentioned in issue #20867

As far as I know, the PortableApps version does not compile Wireshark separately; the same compiled application is merely packaged for PortableApps in addition to the other packaging types (NSIS, WiX on Windows). The PortableApps launcher sets an environment variable, but I do not see how this `PORTABLE` define would ever be defined, so this doesn't do anything at all currently.
This would completely break automatic updates for our Windows NSIS and macOS packages. Marking as a draft for now; I would strongly prefer that this not be merged in its current state.

@johnthacker @geraldcombs Thanks for the clarification it makes sense. I didn’t realize that PortableApps uses the same compiled binary and that PORTABLE is not defined at build time. My intention was only to prevent portable-style packages from using the installer update mechanism, but I see now that this approach is not corret.c I will rework this or look for a better way to detect portable packaging (e.g. via runtime checks or packaging-specific logic), or close this MR if there isn’t a clean solution.

Where is this documented, that "PORTABLEAPPS.com" exists as the way to distinguish this?

I have updated the comment to clarify the purpose of `is_portableapp()`.\
The PortableApps launcher sets the environment variable `"PORTABLEAPPS.com"` when starting apps.\
This is launcher-specific and not part of standard Windows.\
Reference:https://github.com/PortableApps/Launcher

I wonder if it would make more sense to look for the [PortableApps directory layout](https://portableapps.com/manuals/PortableApps.comLauncher/ref/paf/layout.html), e.g. check to see if the parent of `get_progfile_dir()` is named "Wireshark" and that a directory named "AppInfo" sits alongside the "Wireshark" directory. That seems more localized than checking for an environment variable.
